event_type.format: One fixed word, case-sensitive; AwsApiCall on the ordinary calls in this sample.
event_type.quote: Identifies the type of event that generated the event record.

AwsApiCall.meaning: An API was called: the ordinary record, all four samples here.

AwsServiceEvent.meaning: A service generated the event on its own; no caller sent this request.

AwsConsoleAction.meaning: Something done in the console that was not an API call.

AwsConsoleSignIn.meaning: A sign-in to the AWS Management Console.

AwsVpceEvents.meaning: A network activity event recorded for a VPC endpoint owner who enabled network activity events.

examples.note: eventName StartInstances, StopInstances, CreateUser and UpdateTrail in this sample

event_category.format: One fixed word: Management, Data or NetworkActivity.

Management.meaning: A management event; all four samples here.

Data.meaning: A data event, for example an S3 object or Lambda invocation call.

NetworkActivity.meaning: A network activity event recorded through a VPC endpoint.

examples.note: every record in this sample

identity_type.format: One fixed word, case-sensitive; IAMUser on every record in this sample.

Root.meaning: The request was made with the AWS account's own root credentials.

IAMUser.meaning: The request was made with the credentials of an IAM user.

AssumedRole.meaning: The request used temporary credentials from an STS AssumeRole call.

Role.meaning: The request used a persistent IAM identity whose session issuer is always the role.

FederatedUser.meaning: The request used temporary credentials from an STS GetFederationToken call.

Directory.meaning: The request was made to a directory service and the type is otherwise unknown.

AWSAccount.meaning: The request came from another AWS account assuming a role you own.

AWSService.meaning: The request came from an AWS account belonging to an AWS service.

IdentityCenterUser.meaning: The request was made on behalf of an IAM Identity Center user.

Unknown.meaning: CloudTrail could not determine the identity type.

trail_name.format: A trail name (3 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, periods, underscores or dashes) or a trail ARN.

examples.note: the UpdateTrail-by-Terry example, a name that did not resolve

created_user_create_date.format: A human-readable date string. The IAM API reference types CreateDate as ISO 8601, but CloudTrail logs it in this other format.

examples.note: the CreateUser-by-Mary example, not ISO 8601 unlike eventTime

request_id.format: A string the calling service assigns; no fixed shape across services. responseElements.requestId, where present, was byte-identical to the top-level requestID in this sample, though CloudTrail's docs do not state the two always match.

examples.note: requestID and responseElements.requestId, both, on the StartInstances example

instance_id.format: An EC2 instance id string, i- followed by hex digits.

examples.note: named in both requestParameters and responseElements on the StartInstances example

created_user_id.format: A stable, unique IAM id string, 16 to 128 word characters. Not the caller's own principalId: this is the id CreateUser assigned to the user it just made.

examples.note: the CreateUser-by-Mary example, the new user Richard's id

error_code.format: An AWS service exception name, not a numeric code.

TrailNotFoundException.meaning: UpdateTrail was called with a trail name or ARN that does not exist.

examples.note: the UpdateTrail-by-Terry example

event_name.format: The API action name; unbounded across every AWS service, four distinct values in this sample.

StartInstances.meaning: Starts stopped EC2 instances; the aws ec2 start-instances example.

StopInstances.meaning: Stops running EC2 instances; the aws ec2 stop-instances example.

CreateUser.meaning: Creates a new IAM user; the aws iam create-user example.

UpdateTrail.meaning: Updates a trail's settings; the aws cloudtrail update-trail example, shown here failing on an unknown trail.
